name: Kainji Hydroelectric Power Station
summary: Nigeria's first major hydro plant (760 MW), on the Niger at Kainji Dam.
description: Commissioned in 1968, Kainji was the centrepiece of post-independence power expansion. Twelve turbine units draw from Kainji Lake. Two further 110 MW units are being installed to raise the station to 980 MW. Output fluctuates with river flow and rehabilitation works.

name: Zungeru Hydroelectric Power Station
summary: 700 MW plant on the Kaduna River — Nigeria's newest major hydro asset.
description: Built between 2013 and 2023 with Chinese financing and first evacuated onto the grid in 2024. At 700 MW it is among the largest single hydro installations in Nigeria and now carries the highest availability of any grid plant.
operator: Zungeru Hydropower Consortium / Mainstream Energy Solutions Ltd

name: Shiroro Hydroelectric Power Station
summary: 600 MW plant on the Kaduna River in Niger State.
description: Shiroro Dam impounds the Kaduna River gorge east of Minna. The 600 MW plant is among Nigeria's most reliable hydro assets and supports the northern grid.

name: Jebba Hydroelectric Power Station
summary: 578 MW plant on the Niger downstream of Kainji, between Niger and Kwara states.
description: Jebba Dam regulates Niger flow for a 578 MW station operated downstream of Kainji. The dam itself straddles the Niger and Kwara state boundary. It is a key link in the Niger cascade and supports grid stability in central Nigeria.

name: Obudu Dam Hydroelectric Station
summary: 70 MW plant in Cross River State supporting the southeast grid.
description: Obudu Dam on the Cross River system provides peaking power and supports tourism in the Obudu Plateau area. It is among the smaller but strategically placed hydro assets in the south.
gridConnectedNote: Regional dam scheme — not connected to the national grid.

name: Ikere Gorge Hydroelectric Station
summary: 60 MW plant on the Ogun River in Oyo State.
description: Ikere Gorge Dam impounds the Ogun River for power generation and downstream flow regulation. It complements Asejire further upstream on the Oshun/Ogun system.
gridConnectedNote: Regional dam scheme — not connected to the national grid.

name: Dadin Kowa Hydroelectric Power Station
summary: 40 MW plant on the Gongola River in Gombe State.
description: Dadin Kowa hydro uses the Dadin Kowa reservoir to generate power for the northeast grid while supplying irrigation water downstream. Licensed to Mabon Limited.
highlights: Only grid hydro plant in the northeast

name: Challawa Gorge Hydroelectric Station
summary: 39 MW plant on the Challawa River in Kano State.
description: Challawa Gorge Dam supports Kano basin irrigation and runs a 39 MW hydro station. It is part of the broader Hadejia–Jama'are water management system.
gridConnectedNote: Regional dam scheme — not connected to the national grid.

name: Tiga Hydroelectric Power Station
summary: 20 MW plant on the Hadejia River in Kano State.
description: Tiga Dam was built in the 1970s for irrigation and includes a 20 MW hydro station. It is upstream of Challawa in the Hadejia–Jama'are basin.
gridConnectedNote: Regional dam scheme — not connected to the national grid.

name: Goronyo Dam Power & Irrigation
summary: Sokoto basin dam primarily for irrigation and water supply.
description: Goronyo Dam regulates the Rima River for dry-season farming in Sokoto State. While primarily an irrigation asset, it is listed among Nigeria's major water-control structures.
operator: Sokoto Rima River Basin Development Authority
gridConnectedNote: Regional dam scheme — not connected to the national grid.

name: Bakolori Dam
summary: Controversial Sokoto irrigation dam on the Sokoto River.
description: Bakolori Dam was built for irrigated wheat and rice schemes in Sokoto State. It became notable for downstream community displacement and water-access disputes, and is studied in Nigerian environmental history.
operator: Sokoto Rima River Basin Development Authority
gridConnectedNote: Regional dam scheme — not connected to the national grid.

name: Asejire Dam
summary: Multipurpose dam supplying Ibadan; linked to Asejire reservoir.
description: Asejire Dam primarily provides raw water for Ibadan and irrigation in the Oshun valley. It is a key urban water asset for southwestern Nigeria.
gridConnectedNote: Regional dam scheme — not connected to the national grid.

name: Afam Power Complex
summary: 1,556 MW of gas generation at Okoloma-Afam, Oyigbo, Rivers State.
description: Three separate plants share the Afam site: Afam I (Transcorp Power, 726 MW of open-cycle gas turbines from 1982 and 2002), Afam VI (Shell's 650 MW combined cycle, 2010) and the 180 MW Afam II block inaugurated in 2025 by Sahara Power, First Independent Power and Crescendough.
units: Afam I 726 MW, Afam VI 650 MW, Afam II 180 MW
operator: Transcorp Power Plc, Shell Petroleum Development Co, Sahara Power / FIPL

name: Olorunsogo Power Station
summary: 1,085 MW at Olorunsogo, Ewekoro, Ogun State.
description: Eight 42 MW open-cycle units commissioned in 2007, later joined by a 750 MW combined-cycle plant commissioned in February 2015. The combined cycle is the single largest gas build in the National Integrated Power Project programme.
units: Olorunsogo I 335 MW, Olorunsogo II 750 MW
operator: Pacific Energy Company Ltd, Olorunsogo Generation Company Ltd
highlights: Feeds the Lagos and Ogun transmission ring

name: Okpai Power Station
summary: 480 MW combined-cycle plant at Kwale, near Warri, Delta State.
description: Operated by Nigerian Agip Oil Company and built in 2005 as one of Nigeria's three pre-reform independent power projects. It was the first combined-cycle plant in the country and runs on associated Obiafu-Obrikom gas.
operator: Nigerian Agip Oil Company Ltd (Oando PLC)

name: Ihovbor Power Station
summary: 961 MW at Ihovbor, Benin City, Edo State.
description: Two open-cycle blocks built for the National Integrated Power Project: 500 MW commissioned around 2012 and a further 461 MW unit group alongside it. Supply comes from the Escravos-Lagos pipeline system.
highlights: 961 MW at one Edo State site
Connects into Benin North and Ajaokuta

name: Ughelli Power Station (Delta)
summary: Transcorp's 900 MW gas complex at Ughelli, the oldest large thermal site in Nigeria.
description: Commissioned from the late 1960s and expanded with six 100 MW units from 1991. Now operated by Transcorp Power Plc. Ughelli anchors the western end of the Delta-Port Harcourt 330 kV backbone.
highlights: Western anchor of the Delta-Port Harcourt 330 kV line

name: Geregu Power Station
summary: 870 MW at Geregu, Ajaokuta LGA, Kogi State.
description: Two open-cycle blocks each of 435 MW on the Oben-Geregu gas pipeline. Geregu II is part of the National Integrated Power Project programme and feeds the Ajaokuta and Lokoja transmission nodes on the Niger bend.
operator: Amperion Power Distribution Co Ltd, Geregu Power Plc

name: Omotosho Power Station
summary: 835 MW at Omotosho, Odigbo, Ondo State.
description: Eight 42 MW units commissioned in 2005, followed by a 500 MW open-cycle block in 2012. Omotosho feeds the Omotosho-Epe-Ajah 330 kV corridor that links the coastal plants into the Lagos ring.
units: Omotosho I 335 MW, Omotosho II 500 MW
operator: Omotosho Power Plc, Omotosho Generation Company Ltd
highlights: Evacuates over the Omotosho-Epe-Ajah 330 kV line

name: Odukpani Power Station (Calabar)
summary: 625 MW at Odukpani, Calabar, Cross River State.
description: Five gas turbine units commissioned in 2015 for the National Integrated Power Project. Odukpani is the main generation source for the Calabar and southern Cross River corridor.
highlights: Feeds the Cross River and Akwa Ibom load centres

name: Alaoji Power Station
summary: 500 MW at Alaoji, Obo, Abia State.
description: Four 124 MW open-cycle gas turbines built for the National Integrated Power Project and licensed around 2012-2015. Alaoji injects into the Alaoji-Onitsha 330 kV line that carries Imo and Abia load toward the southeast corridor.
highlights: Injects on the Alaoji-Onitsha 330 kV line

name: Ibom Power Station
summary: 190 MW at Ikot Abasi, Akwa Ibom State.
description: Two GE Frame 6B and one Frame 9E gas turbines in open-cycle configuration, commissioned in 2009 and owned by the Akwa Ibom State Government. It is the principal grid source for the Uyo and Ikot Abasi load centre.
units: 2 x 63 MW Frame 6B, 1 x 63 MW Frame 9E
highlights: Main source for the Uyo load centre
Three gas turbines in simple cycle

name: Omoku Power Station
summary: 150 MW at Omoku, Rivers State.
description: Licensed to First Independent Power in the 2000s and operating on the Trans-Amadi-Omoku corridor inland from Port Harcourt. A larger second phase at the same site has remained incomplete.

name: Trans-Amadi Power Station
summary: 100 MW at Trans-Amadi industrial district, Port Harcourt.
description: Phase II of the FIPL site, four 25 MW gas turbines commissioned in 2009 with Shell gas supply. Sited inside the Trans-Amadi industrial estate, so it serves heavy industry rather than the wider network.
highlights: Phase II of the FIPL Trans-Amadi site

name: Egbin Power Station
summary: Nigeria's largest thermal plant — 1,320 MW at Ijede, Ikorodu, Lagos.
description: Six 220 MW steam turbine units commissioned between 1985 and 1987. Egbin is the single biggest contributor to national generation and sits at the head of the Lagos 330 kV transmission ring. Privatised in 2013 to Sahara Group and KEPCO.
highlights: Head of the Lagos 330 kV ring

name: Sapele Power Station
type: Gas-fired steam station and OCGT plant
summary: 1,220 MW at Sapele, Delta State — steam units plus the newer Sapele II turbines.
description: Phase one consists of six 120 MW gas-fired steam units commissioned from 1978, two of which are mothballed. Sapele II added four 113 MW open-cycle gas turbines in 2012. Both blocks sit on the Escravos gas pipeline system.
operator: Sapele Power Plc, Ogorode Generation Company Ltd
highlights: Fed from the Escravos pipeline system

name: Abuja Electricity Distribution Plc (AEDC)
summary: DisCo for the Federal Capital Territory and adjoining north-central states.
description: AEDC distributes grid power across the FCT and Niger, Kogi and Nasarawa states from its Abuja headquarters, serving residential, government and industrial load centres on the Abuja-Lokoja-Minna corridor.
shareholding: Core Infrastructure Investment, FCT and Kogi state governments

name: Benin Electricity Distribution Plc (BEDC)
summary: South-south and southwest DisCo covering Edo, Delta, Ekiti and Ondo.
description: BEDC operates from Benin City, distributing electricity across the Niger Delta fringe and the Edo-Ekiti-Ondo axis, including major cities such as Benin, Warri, Asaba, Akure and Ado-Ekiti.
shareholding: Infrastructure Trust Fund (Amethi), BEDC staff and state governments

name: Eko Electricity Distribution Plc (EKEDP)
summary: Southern Lagos franchise DisCo, also serving Agbara in Ogun State.
description: EKEDP covers the southern part of Lagos State across twelve districts including Lekki, Apapa, Islands and Ajah, plus Agbara in Ogun State. It takes bulk supply from the Ajah and Akangba 330/132 kV transmission nodes.
shareholding: Kekehohoduke family and Arise Integrated Industrial Platforms

name: Enugu Electricity Distribution Plc (EEDC)
summary: Southeast DisCo for the five Igbo heartland states.
description: EEDC distributes power across Enugu, Abia, Imo, Anambra and Ebonyi from Enugu, anchoring the eastern grid's urban and industrial consumers.
shareholding: Stanbic IBTC, Access Holdings and Enugu State Government

name: Ibadan Electricity Distribution Plc (IBEDC)
summary: Southwest DisCo covering Oyo, Ogun, Osun, Kwara and parts of Ekiti, Kogi and Niger.
description: IBEDC has the largest franchise area in Nigeria, covering Oyo, Ogun, Osun and Kwara plus parts of Ekiti, Kogi and Niger. It is organised into five regions and is the biggest DisCo by customer count.
shareholding: Ibadan Electricity Distribution Holding and Fashola Sanusi consortium

name: Ikeja Electric Plc (IE)
summary: Mainland and northern Lagos franchise DisCo.
description: Ikeja Electric serves mainland Lagos, Ikeja, Oshodi and the northern Lagos industrial corridors from its Ikeja headquarters, complementing EKEDP's southern and island franchise. It bills the highest revenue of any DisCo.
shareholding: Consortium led by Access Holdings, Arthur Jarvis and Stephen Jennings

name: Jos Electricity Distribution Plc (JEDC)
summary: Middle Belt DisCo for Plateau, Bauchi, Benue and Gombe.
description: JEDC distributes electricity from Jos across the Plateau highlands and into Bauchi, Benue and Gombe, serving mining towns, universities and farming communities.
shareholding: MIH Holdings and Broad Street Investments

name: Kaduna Electricity Distribution Plc (KAEDCO)
summary: Northwest DisCo for Kaduna, Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara.
description: KAEDCO operates from Kaduna city, distributing power across the northwestern savanna states with major load centres in Kaduna, Zaria, Sokoto and Gusau.
shareholding: Kaduna State Government, Federal Government and APTN staff

name: Kano Electricity Distribution Plc (KEDCO)
summary: Northwest DisCo for Kano, Katsina and Jigawa.
description: KEDCO distributes electricity from Kano across Nigeria's most populous northern metropolis and into Jigawa and Katsina, including major markets and textile clusters.
shareholding: Kano State Government and Smart Energy International

name: Port Harcourt Electricity Distribution Plc (PHEDC)
summary: South-south DisCo for Rivers, Bayelsa, Cross River and Akwa Ibom.
description: PHEDC operates from Port Harcourt, distributing power across the Niger Delta oil cities and the eastern coastal states, including major industrial and export facilities.
shareholding: Crown Trust Asset Management and APTN staff

name: Yola Electricity Distribution Plc (YEDC)
summary: Northeast DisCo for Adamawa, Taraba, Borno and Yobe.
description: YEDC distributes grid power from Yola across the northeast savanna and Sahel fringe, including state capitals and agricultural towns in Adamawa, Taraba, Borno and Yobe.
shareholding: Revrest Financial Partners and Yola Electricity Distribution staff
